questions.statement: Which sentence expresses a possibility of about fifty per cent?
questions.context: Modales de posibilidad, San Juan, grado 11.

options.text: It may rain later this afternoon.
options.feedback: 'May' is a standard possibility form and is also acceptable here.

options.text: It must rain later this afternoon.
options.feedback: 'Must' expresses strong deduction, not a fifty per cent chance.

options.text: It might rain later this afternoon.
options.feedback: 'Might' suggests a lower probability than 'may'.

options.text: It cannot rain later this afternoon.
options.feedback: 'Cannot' expresses impossibility.

questions.explanation:
'May' expresa posibilidad en general, mientras 'might' sugiere una probabilidad menor.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'You ____ be right, but I doubt it.' The speaker thinks it is unlikely.

options.feedback: 'Must' would assert certainty.
'Should' expresses expectation or recommendation, not the speaker's doubt.
'Will' is a future auxiliary and carries no hedging function.
'Might' conveys the speaker's own low confidence in the statement.

questions.explanation:
Una conjetura que el hablante considera poco probable se expresa con 'might be'. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'must' mean in the sentence 'She must be exhausted; she has been working all day'?

options.text: The speaker is giving an order
options.feedback: An order requires a different pattern, not this declarative use.

options.text: The speaker is almost certain, based on the evidence
options.feedback: 'Must' marks a deduction from the facts given.

options.text: The speaker is not certain at all
options.feedback: That reading would require 'might' or 'could'.

options.text: The speaker is certain the opposite is true
options.feedback: 'Cannot' would express that reading instead.

questions.explanation:
En presente, 'must' expresa una conclusion logica a partir de la evidencia disponible.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that uses 'cannot' correctly.

options.text: That cannot be true; the numbers do not match.
options.feedback: 'Cannot be' expresses that the situation is impossible.

options.text: That can not be true is obvious.
options.feedback: Splitting 'cannot' and inverting the order breaks the grammar.

options.text: That cannot be true is obvious.
options.feedback: The word order after 'cannot' is inverted without cause.
The progressive is not compatible with this modal use.

questions.explanation:
'Cannot' expresa imposibilidad y mantiene el mismo orden que los demas modales. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'You ____ have told me earlier; I would have cancelled the trip.'

options.feedback: 'Would have' describes an unreal past result, not a reproach.
'Should have' expresses reproach about something not done in the past.
'Can have' does not carry that function.
'Must have' would express a deduction about the past, not blame.

questions.explanation:
La expresion reprocha una omision pasada, asi que el modal corresponde al pasado: 'should have'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'could' and 'was able to'?

options.text: 'Could' is general ability; 'was able to' is a specific past occasion
options.feedback: 'Was able to' points to one realised instance.

options.text: They mean exactly the same thing in every context
options.feedback: They overlap in many sentences but differ in this focus.
'Could' is common in statements as well.

options.text: 'Was able to' refers to the future
options.feedback: 'Was able to' is a past form.

questions.explanation:
'Could' expresa habilidad general o posibilidad, mientras 'was able to' se refiere a un caso concreto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'You may want to check the figures before the meeting.' What is the speaker doing?

options.feedback: An order would use 'must' or 'have to'.

options.text: Expressing a doubt about the figures
options.feedback: 'May' here softens the suggestion rather than expressing doubt.

options.text: Making a prediction about the meeting
options.feedback: No future prediction is made in the sentence.
'May want to' softens the advice so the listener can decide.

questions.explanation:
'May want to' expresa una sugerencia prudente al oyente sin imponerla. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'She ____ be at the office by now; she left an hour ago.'
questions.context: Deduccion sobre el presente, Vega Baja, grado 11.

options.feedback: 'Might' would weaken a deduction the speaker considers solid.
'Should' expresses expectation, which is weaker than the evidence warrants here.
'Must be' expresses the deduction the evidence supports.
'Will' is a future auxiliary and carries no deductive meaning.

questions.explanation:
Los datos apresentados sostienen una conclusion logica en presente, que corresponde a 'must be'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses certainty about a past situation?

options.feedback: The bare infinitive refers to a present or future obligation.

options.text: He will have forget the appointment.
options.feedback: The future perfect requires a participle, not the base form.
That sequence is not grammatical.

options.text: He must have forgotten the appointment.
options.feedback: 'Must have' plus participle marks a firm conclusion about the past.

questions.explanation:
'Must have' seguido de participio expresa una conclusion firme sobre el pasado. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'She must to leave early.' What is the error?

options.feedback: Modal verbs are followed directly by the base form.

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: The infinitive after 'must' is a standard error.
Neither modal takes an infinitive, so that change would not fix it.
After a modal the base form is required, not the -ing form.

questions.explanation:
Tras un modal no se usa 'to' ni ningun otro auxiliar. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'I ____ rather stay at home tonight.'

options.feedback: 'Will rather' is not a standard construction.
'Must' expresses obligation, not preference.
'Could rather' is not idiomatic in this position.
'Would rather' expresses a preference between two options.

questions.explanation:
'Would rather' expresa preferencia y va seguido de la forma base del verbo. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'have to' correctly?

options.text: Students must to wear a uniform at this school.
options.feedback: No infinitive may follow a modal verb.

options.text: Students are having to wear a uniform to school.
options.feedback: The progressive is not used with 'have to' in this meaning.

options.text: Students have to wear a uniform at this school.
options.feedback: 'Have to' marks an externally imposed obligation.

options.text: Students have wear a uniform at this school.
options.feedback: 'Have' requires the base form, not the bare infinitive.

questions.explanation:
'Have to' expresa obligacion externa impuesta por una norma o una tercera persona. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: Read: 'The concert may be sold out by tonight.' What can you conclude?
questions.context: Inferencia sobre una prediccion, Naguabo, grado 11.

options.text: There is a chance that all tickets have been sold
options.feedback: 'May' keeps the possibility open without confirming it.

options.text: All tickets have certainly been sold
options.feedback: Certainty would require 'must be' or a plain statement.
'Cannot be sold out' would express that reading.
No mention of a cancellation appears in the sentence.

questions.explanation:
'May be' deja abierta la posibilidad de que ya no queden entradas, sin asegurarlo. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'You ____ have seen the doctor; you look feverish.'

options.feedback: 'Must have' would turn the recommendation into a deduction.
'Can have' does not express advice.
'Should have seen' is a recommendation about what ought to have happened.
'Will have' is a future perfect form with no advisory sense.

questions.explanation:
'Should' expresa recomendacion y no una afirmacion sobre el pasado. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT correct?
questions.context: Revision de modales, Juana Diaz, grado 11.

options.text: I would like a cup of coffee.
options.feedback: The fixed expression 'would like' is complete here.

options.text: I would a cup of coffee like.
options.feedback: The auxiliary 'would' cannot be separated from 'like'.

options.text: I would like to have a cup of coffee.
options.feedback: 'Would like to' plus the infinitive is correct.

options.text: I would like a coffee cup.
options.feedback: 'Would like' plus a noun phrase is also correct.

questions.explanation:
Las dos palabras 'would like' funcionan como un bloque y no deben separarse por un sustantivo.

questions.statement: What does 'ought to' express?

options.feedback: 'Ought to have' covers the past, but the plain form is present.
That is 'must have'.
'Ought to' is the formal equivalent of 'should'.

options.text: Probability of about fifty per cent
options.feedback: That is 'may' or 'might'.

questions.explanation:
'Ought to' expresa obligacion o recomendacion y equivale a 'should'. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'You ____ not smoke in the hospital; it is against the rules.'

options.feedback: 'Should not' would express advice rather than a prohibition.
'Might not' expresses a low probability, not a rule.
'Could not' expresses inability rather than prohibition.
'Must not' expresses a prohibition grounded in a rule.

questions.explanation:
Una prohibicion formulada con 'must' se expresa en negativo con 'must not'. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports a past obligation?

options.text: We should leave earlier to avoid the traffic.
options.feedback: The bare 'should' refers to the present or future.

options.text: We should have left earlier to avoid the traffic.
options.feedback: 'Should have' expresses a past obligation that was not met.

options.text: We will have left earlier to avoid the traffic.
options.feedback: The future perfect refers to a future reference point.

options.text: We must have left earlier to avoid the traffic.
options.feedback: 'Must have' would express a deduction, not an obligation.

questions.explanation:
'Should have' u 'ought to have' expresa una obligacion retrospectiva sobre algo no hecho.

questions.statement: Read the sentence: 'He can play three languages, but he cannot write in all of them.' What does the modal convey?

options.text: Ability that exists in one direction but not the other
options.feedback: 'Can' grants the skill and 'cannot' withholds it in writing.

options.text: A possibility that depends on time
options.feedback: 'Can' expresses ability here, not a temporal condition.
Prohibition would require a modal of obligation, not 'cannot' as ability.
Past deduction requires 'must have'.

questions.explanation:
La pareja 'can' y 'cannot' delimita hasta donde llega la capacidad del hablante. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that uses 'might' in the correct register and form.
questions.context: Registro y forma, Vega Baja, grado 11.

options.text: You might wanting to reconsider the offer.
options.feedback: The -ing form cannot follow a modal verb.

options.text: You might want to reconsider the offer.
options.feedback: 'Might' hedges the suggestion politely and is fully standard.

options.text: You might to reconsider the offer.
options.feedback: No infinitive marker may follow a modal.
The base form must follow the modal.

questions.explanation:
'Might' es la forma correcta para expresar una posibilidad menor y suena mas diplomático que 'may'.
